architecturalFinding.detail: PipelineResult.errors has EXACTLY ONE write site repo-wide: PgeEngine.run (src/pge/engine/pge-engine.ts:551-572), spreading errors from the interpreter's own TaskFailure records, only when failures.length>0. That code and its doc comment PRE-DATE this sprint — introduced in spec-20260812-pge-real-workload-errors sprint 5 — and this sprint's diff does not touch the PipelineResult interface at all. The divergence was previously MASKED because contracts/version was also diverging under the same pipelineResult field name; nobody had isolated the container portion from the whole. Imperative equivalent: runSprintCycle's auto-commit (pipeline.ts:449-462) calls commitAll UNCONDITIONALLY when autoCommit is true, in a try/catch that only debug-logs and continues — no HITL gate at all. finalizePipelineRun requests the end-of-pipeline checkpoint AFTER the marker and history event are written and does not gate on its outcome. The graph, by contrast, has an explicit hitl_commit node (coding.graph.ts:911-923) feeding a separate commit node (:926-937) — 'reachable only behind the approval gate, which is what makes the git effect blockable fail-closed'. So fabricating an errors entry would misreport an event the imperative architecture CANNOT produce, and adding errors to VOLATILE_KEYS would violate that set's own documented bar ('a key belongs here only when two runs of the SAME engine over the same input would differ on it' — errors differs BETWEEN engines on the SAME input, exactly the class VOLATILE_KEYS must not hide).
